Branch feat/global-settings-tier (7 pushed commits, tip 2b81a7acb). ONE new commit, no amending. Read CLAUDE.md first.

## Context

The branch adds "invisible routing": for globally-tracked repos (no repo-level .entire setup), runtime paths (.entire/{metadata,logs,tmp}) resolve under <git-common-dir>/entire/worktree/ via paths.AbsPath interception (paths/invisible.go). Three findings from trail review:

## Finding 1 (HIGH, trail 019fee6e-f8a4): invisible base is shared across linked worktrees; migration steals other worktrees' data

`invisibleRuntimeBase` routes ALL worktrees of a clone to the same `<git-common-dir>/entire/worktree/...` (pinned by TestAbsPath_InvisibleRouting_LinkedWorktree). Consequences: (a) two globally-tracked worktrees of one clone interleave logs and could collide; (b) `maybeMigrateGlobalRuntimeData` (setup_global.go) unconditionally moves the ENTIRE shared dir into whichever worktree runs `entire enable` first — including another worktree's in-flight session metadata.

Fix: namespace the invisible base PER WORKTREE, matching the repo's established worktree-isolation precedent — shadow branches use a worktree hash (see strategy shadow-branch naming, `entire/<commit>-<worktreeHash[:6]>`) and paths.GetWorktreeID exists (paths/worktree.go). Choose the established stable identifier (prefer the same worktree-hash derivation shadow branches use — find it in strategy/ and reuse/export rather than invent; if it lives awkwardly, paths.GetWorktreeID is acceptable — justify your choice in the commit message). New layout: `<git-common-dir>/entire/worktree/<worktree-key>/{metadata,logs,tmp}`. Update: invisible.go base construction + its cache key if needed; maybeMigrateGlobalRuntimeData to migrate ONLY the current worktree's namespace (leave other namespaces untouched); doctor's globally-tracked checks if they reference the path; ALL affected tests including the linked-worktree test (which must now pin ISOLATION: two worktrees get different bases under the same common dir) and the migration tests. Nothing is released yet — no back-compat shim for the un-namespaced layout is needed, but grep for any other reference to "entire/worktree" to catch stragglers.

## Finding 2 (HIGH, trail 019fee43-9948): doctor/trace diagnostics look in the worktree location only

doctor_logs.go, doctor_bundle.go, trace_cmd.go build log paths as `filepath.Join(repoRoot, logging.LogsDir, ...)` directly — for globally-tracked repos the logs live under the git common dir, so `entire doctor logs/bundle/trace` silently report nothing for exactly the repos this feature targets. Fix: resolve through paths.AbsPath (which routes correctly for both modes). Locate every such call site in those three files (grep `logging.LogsDir` and `.entire/logs` across cmd/) and convert; add one test per command path proving a globally-tracked repo's logs are found (follow each file's existing test patterns).

## Finding 3 (MEDIUM, trail 019fee43-9b6f): review context misses prompts in globally-tracked repos

`formatReviewSessionLine` in review_context.go builds the prompt path as `filepath.Join(worktreeRoot, paths.SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID(...), paths.PromptFileName)` — misses the routed location, silently dropping the in-progress-session section from `entire review`. Fix: route through paths.AbsPath. Check the same file for sibling direct joins of metadata paths and convert those too. Test: prompt readable in a globally-tracked repo fixture.

## Rules

TDD where practical; every converted call site needs the failing-then-passing demonstration OR an existing test extended. Before commit: mise run fmt && mise run lint (rerun after fmt if rewritten) && mise run test && mise run test:integration && mise run test:e2e:canary (invisible-routing layout changed — canary required). ONE commit: "fix(global): per-worktree invisible routing + route diagnostics through AbsPath" style message listing the three findings by trail ID, Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>.

Self-review focus: the namespacing change touches the feature's core promise — re-verify the integration test still proves byte-clean git status, and that migration in a two-worktree fixture moves ONLY the enabling worktree's namespace (write exactly that test).

Report: DONE/etc; worktree-key choice + rationale; files; test lines; commit SHA; anything the namespacing broke that you had to adapt.

712	# Important Notes
713	
714	- **Before committing:** Follow the "Before Every Commit (REQUIRED)" checklist above - CI will fail without it
715	- Integration tests: run `mise run test:integration` when changing integration test code
716	- When adding new features, ensure they are well-tested and documented.
717	- Always check for code duplication and refactor as needed.
718	
719	## Tests and Comments
720	
721	- Tests are not required merely because production code changed. Add or modify tests only when they protect meaningful observable behavior, a non-trivial invariant or boundary, or a concrete regression.
722	- Before adding a test, identify the realistic regression it would catch and why existing coverage would not catch it. If the only rationale is coverage, symmetry, or "the code changed," omit the test.
723	- Do not add tombstone tests whose only purpose is to assert that removed code, routes, fields, or features remain absent. Negative tests are appropriate when the failure or absence is itself a current API, security, or persistence contract.
724	- Avoid tests that merely mirror literal values, declarative mappings, obvious control flow, or implementation details. For diagnostics and other structured user-visible output, prefer the repository's established UI, snapshot, or integration coverage over redundant partial-string assertions.
725	- Prefer extending an existing test at the appropriate behavior boundary over adding a new test file, fixture, helper, or test-only abstraction. Do not build test infrastructure that is more complex or brittle than the behavior under test.

727	- Do not add comments or doc comments that merely restate the code, symbol name, test name, file or module purpose, or obvious control flow. Prefer clearer naming and structure.
